title: Découverte tactile: Qu'est-ce qu'une texture?
oneGoal: Les élèves explorent différentes textures par le toucher sécuritaire et apprennent à décrire ce qu'ils ressentent
progression: Leçon de base : Introduction à la découverte sensorielle et à la description des textures

opening.activity: Texture Mystery Bags: Students feel different textured materials in cloth bags without looking. Start with very different textures (sandpaper vs silk fabric vs sponge). Use exaggerated facial expressions and sounds to model reactions: 'Ooh, c'est rugueux!' Make texture vocabulary come alive through dramatic touch reactions.

required.preparation: Vérifier solidité coutures, laver avant usage

required.specifics: Laine feutrée, bois lisse, coton doux, toile de jute, mousse, carton ondulé
required.preparation: Découper taille sécuritaire (>5cm), nettoyer tous matériaux
required.safety: ✓ Pas d'échardes ✓ Pas d'allergènes ✓ Taille appropriée
removed_unsafe: Papier sablé (trop abrasif pour peau Grade 1)

opening.visualSupports: Échantillons de textures étiquetés (rugueux, lisse, doux, dur), tableaux de réaction de l'enseignant
movementBreaks: Dance to show how textures make you feel
Move paintbrush arms in big circles

main.activity: Texture Exploration Stations: Set up 5 stations with different texture families. Station 1: Rough textures (sandpaper, bark, burlap). Station 2: Smooth textures (silk, plastic, metal spoon). Station 3: Soft textures (cotton balls, velvet, fur fabric). Station 4: Hard textures (wooden blocks, stones, ceramic tiles). Station 5: Bumpy textures (bubble wrap, corrugated cardboard, textured rollers). Students rotate every 5 minutes, practicing vocabulary and safe touching techniques.

required.item: Matériaux de stations de texture organisés
required.quantity: 5 bacs avec matériaux par famille (rugueux, lisse, doux, dur, bosselé)
required.preparation: Organiser par catégorie, étiqueter clairement chaque bac

required.quantity: Papier sablé, écorce, toile rugueuse, pierre ponce
required.preparation: Vérifier sécurité - pas trop abrasif pour enfants
Nettoyer, s'assurer pas de bords coupants

required.quantity: Boules de coton, velours, fourrure synthétique, peluche
Blocs de bois, pierres, carreaux céramique, métal
required.preparation: Vérifier absence d'arêtes vives, taille adaptée

required.quantity: Papier bulle, carton ondulé, rouleaux texturés
1 minuteur réglé sur 5 minutes par station

safety.preparation: Accessible et facile d'usage pour enfants

main.visualSupports: Station instruction cards with texture vocabulary, safe touching technique posters
decisionPoints: Decision Point 1: Observe sensory exploration. If overwhelmed by textures, limit choices; if engaged, introduce contrasting materials.
Decision Point 2: Monitor vocabulary development. If struggling with texture words, use gestures and modeling; if confident, encourage descriptive language.
Decision Point 3: Check artistic application. If random texture use, guide purposeful choices; if thoughtful placement, ask them to explain their decisions.
main.movementBreaks: Texture body movements at 12 and 22 minutes - act out rough (sharp movements), smooth (flowing movements), soft (gentle movements)

closing.activity: Texture Memory Circle: Students sit in circle and each chooses one favorite texture from today. Take turns showing the texture and describing it using new vocabulary: 'C'est doux comme...', 'C'est rugueux comme...'. Create class texture memory by having élèves suggest where they might find similar textures at home or in nature. End with appreciation: 'Merci, nos mains!' (Thank you, our hands!)

required.preparation: Affichage visible pour soutenir l'expression orale

closing.visualSupports: Texture vocabulary reference cards for sharing support
movementBreaks: Dance to show how textures make you feel
Move paintbrush arms in big circles

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students showing texture aversion or sensory overwhelm
troubleshooting.then: Respect individual comfort levels. Offer visual observation instead of touching. Use gentler textures like soft fabric or smooth stones. Allow élèves to wash hands immediately after exploration.

realWorldConnection: Explore textures at home - clothing, furniture, kitchen tools, outdoor surfaces. Families can help identify texture words in home language and French.

pourÉlèvesEnDifficulté: Use larger texture samples that are easier for developing fine motor skills to manipulate
Focus on very different textures (avoid subtle differences) to ensure clear sensory input
Commencer avec des textures douces et familières avant d'introduire des matériaux plus rugueux ou nouveaux
Provide emotional support for any texture discomfort - normalize preferences and sensitivities
pourÉlèvesAvancés: Challenge with subtle texture differences (various paper grits, different fabric weaves)
Introduce texture comparison vocabulary: 'plus rugueux que', 'moins lisse que'
Help peers by demonstrating safe touching techniques and describing complex textures
Begin predicting what objects might feel like before touching them
pourApprenantsFrançais: Connect texture words to objects from their home culture and experiences
Use texture exploration as universal language - touching and feeling cross cultural barriers
Allow description of textures in home language first, then connect to French terms
Focus on sensory experience which doesn't require advanced language skills
pourÉlèvesAvecPEI: Adapt texture materials to individual sensory needs and tolerances
Provide alternative ways to explore textures (visual only, tools for touching)
Allow breaks from sensory input as needed for regulation and comfort
Celebrate any level of texture engagement as meaningful sensory learning

observable: Student demonstrates curiosity and willingness to explore different textures through safe touching
Student uses appropriate vocabulary or gestures to describe texture sensations (rough, smooth, soft, hard)
Student shows respect for materials and follows safe touching techniques during texture exploration
checkpoints: Opening: Student participates in mystery bag exploration with interest and attempts to describe what they feel
Main: Student rotates through texture stations, explores materials safely, practices texture vocabulary appropriately
Closing: Student shares texture discoveries and shows appreciation for their hands as exploration tools
